builtin_checks.title: User Account Control is enabled
builtin_checks.description: User Account Control mediates elevation to administrative rights. With it off, any process started by a member of the local Administrators group runs fully elevated with no prompt and no split token.
builtin_checks.rationale: Disabling UAC removes the boundary that stops a single user-context compromise becoming immediate administrative control of the machine.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set EnableLUA to 1 under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System and restart the host.

builtin_checks.title: RDP requires Network Level Authentication
builtin_checks.description: Network Level Authentication makes the client authenticate before a Remote Desktop session is created.
builtin_checks.rationale: Without NLA the server allocates a session and renders a logon screen to an unauthenticated caller, which both widens the pre-authentication attack surface and makes RDP usable for resource exhaustion.
builtin_checks.remediation: Enable 'Require user authentication for remote connections by using Network Level Authentication', or set UserAuthentication to 1 on the RDP-Tcp listener.

builtin_checks.title: SMBv1 server is disabled
builtin_checks.description: The SMB version 1 server protocol, superseded since 2006 and the transport used by EternalBlue and WannaCry.
builtin_checks.rationale: SMBv1 has no protocol-level integrity protection and cannot negotiate the mitigations later dialects carry.
builtin_checks.remediation: Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName SMB1Protocol, or set SMB1 to 0 under the LanmanServer parameters key.

builtin_checks.title: Anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts is restricted
builtin_checks.description: Controls whether an unauthenticated session may enumerate local account names.
builtin_checks.rationale: An account list is the input to password spraying; withholding it removes the step that makes spraying efficient.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set RestrictAnonymousSAM to 1 under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa.

builtin_checks.title: Windows Firewall service is running
builtin_checks.description: The Windows Defender Firewall service enforces host packet filtering.
builtin_checks.rationale: With the service stopped, every profile's rules are inert and the host accepts whatever the network offers it.
builtin_checks.remediation: Start-Service MpsSvc and set its start type to Automatic.

builtin_checks.title: Telnet server is not installed
builtin_checks.description: The Telnet server service, which carries credentials in clear text.
builtin_checks.rationale: Telnet authenticates over an unencrypted channel; anyone able to observe the path recovers the password.
builtin_checks.remediation: Uninstall the Telnet Server feature and use SSH or WinRM over HTTPS instead.

builtin_checks.title: Remote Registry service is not running
builtin_checks.description: The Remote Registry service allows the registry to be read and written across the network.
builtin_checks.rationale: It is rarely required on a workstation and gives an authenticated attacker a broad configuration read, and often a write.
builtin_checks.remediation: Stop the RemoteRegistry service and set its start type to Disabled where remote management does not depend on it.

builtin_checks.title: Minimum password length is at least 14 characters
builtin_checks.description: The local security policy's minimum password length.
builtin_checks.rationale: Length is the property that most directly resists offline cracking of a recovered hash.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set Minimum password length to 14 or more in the local security policy, or through the domain password policy where the host is joined.

builtin_checks.title: Password history retains at least 24 passwords
builtin_checks.description: How many previous passwords the system refuses to accept again.
builtin_checks.rationale: Without history a forced change can be satisfied by re-setting the password that was just compromised.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set 'Enforce password history' to 24 or more.

builtin_checks.title: Account lockout threshold is set and workable
builtin_checks.description: Failed sign-in attempts before the account is locked.
builtin_checks.rationale: A per-account lockout is the control that answers credential stuffing from many source addresses, which no per-address rate limit can.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set 'Account lockout threshold' to a value between 1 and 10, with a lockout duration long enough to make automated guessing impractical.

builtin_checks.title: SSH does not permit password-based root login
builtin_checks.description: Whether the SSH daemon accepts a direct root login with a password.
builtin_checks.rationale: Direct root login removes the accountability of a named account and gives a single guessed password full control of the host.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set 'PermitRootLogin prohibit-password' (or 'no') in /etc/ssh/sshd_config and reload sshd.

builtin_checks.title: SSH password authentication is disabled
builtin_checks.description: Whether the SSH daemon accepts passwords as well as keys.
builtin_checks.rationale: Key authentication is not guessable; leaving passwords enabled keeps the host exposed to spraying regardless of key hygiene.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set 'PasswordAuthentication no' once key access is confirmed working for every account that needs it.

builtin_checks.title: SSH limits authentication attempts per connection
builtin_checks.description: Failed attempts allowed within a single SSH connection.
builtin_checks.rationale: A high limit lets one connection carry many guesses, which costs an attacker far less than opening a connection per attempt.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set 'MaxAuthTries 4' in /etc/ssh/sshd_config.

builtin_checks.title: /etc/passwd is not group- or world-writable
builtin_checks.description: Filesystem mode of the local account database.
builtin_checks.rationale: A writable /etc/passwd allows an unprivileged user to add an account, or to blank the password field of an existing one.
builtin_checks.remediation: chmod 0644 /etc/passwd && chown root:root /etc/passwd

builtin_checks.title: /etc/shadow is not readable by unprivileged users
builtin_checks.description: Filesystem mode of the local password hash store.
builtin_checks.rationale: A readable /etc/shadow hands every local user the hashes to crack offline, at their own pace and without triggering any lockout.
builtin_checks.remediation: chmod 0640 /etc/shadow && chown root:shadow /etc/shadow

builtin_checks.title: The audit daemon is running
builtin_checks.description: auditd records kernel audit events to disk.
builtin_checks.rationale: Without it there is no local record of privilege use or of changes to the files these other rules check, so an incident cannot be reconstructed afterwards.
builtin_checks.remediation: Install and enable auditd, then define an audit ruleset.

builtin_checks.title: No telnet daemon is listening
builtin_checks.description: TCP 23, the telnet service port.
builtin_checks.rationale: Telnet transmits credentials and session content in clear text on a network where anyone on the path can read them.
builtin_checks.remediation: Remove the telnet server package and use SSH.

builtin_checks.title: Password maximum age is set
builtin_checks.description: PASS_MAX_DAYS from /etc/login.defs.
builtin_checks.rationale: An unbounded password lifetime means a credential compromised years ago is still valid today.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set PASS_MAX_DAYS in /etc/login.defs and apply with chage.

builtin_checks.title: Password quality enforces a minimum length
builtin_checks.description: minlen from /etc/security/pwquality.conf.
builtin_checks.rationale: Length is the property that most directly resists offline cracking of a recovered hash.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set 'minlen = 14' in /etc/security/pwquality.conf.

builtin_checks.title: /etc/crontab is not writable by unprivileged users
builtin_checks.description: Filesystem mode of the system crontab.
builtin_checks.rationale: A writable system crontab is a direct path to code execution as root at the next scheduled run.
builtin_checks.remediation: chmod 0644 /etc/crontab && chown root:root /etc/crontab

builtin_checks.title: No service grants configuration rights to a non-administrator
builtin_checks.description: Every service's security descriptor is read and checked for an access-control entry granting a non-administrative principal the right to change the service's configuration.
builtin_checks.rationale: A principal that can change a service's configuration can point its binary path at anything and restart it. That is SYSTEM on the next start, with no further condition — the shortest path from an ordinary account to full control of the host.
builtin_checks.remediation: Remove CHANGE_CONFIG, WRITE_DAC, WRITE_OWNER and ALL_ACCESS from non-administrative principals on the named services: sc.exe sdset <service> <SDDL>. Only Administrators and SYSTEM should hold them.

builtin_checks.title: No service executable is writable by a non-administrator
builtin_checks.description: The executable behind each service is resolved and its ACL inspected for write access granted to Everyone, Users, Authenticated Users or Guests.
builtin_checks.rationale: Overwriting the binary a service runs replaces what SYSTEM executes at the next start. It needs no other weakness and survives a reboot.
builtin_checks.remediation: Remove write, modify and full-control entries for non-administrative principals from the named executables, and from the directories containing them.

builtin_checks.title: AlwaysInstallElevated is not enabled
builtin_checks.description: Checks whether AlwaysInstallElevated is set to 1 in **both** HKLM and HKCU. Either alone has no effect and is not reported.
builtin_checks.rationale: With both set, any Windows Installer package runs with SYSTEM privileges regardless of who launches it. An unprivileged user who can write an MSI has full control of the host.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set AlwaysInstallElevated to 0, or remove it, under SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer in both HKLM and HKCU.

builtin_checks.title: No service has an exploitable unquoted image path
builtin_checks.description: Services whose image path is unquoted, contains a space, and resolves outside %SystemRoot%. Unquoted paths without a space, and those under %SystemRoot%, are not reported — neither is hijackable.
builtin_checks.rationale: Windows resolves an unquoted path by trying each space-delimited prefix in turn, so C:\Program Files\App\svc.exe will run C:\Program.exe first if it exists. Where an unprivileged user can write to one of those directories, the service runs their binary as SYSTEM.
builtin_checks.remediation: Quote the image path: sc.exe config <service> binPath= "\"C:\Path With Spaces\svc.exe\"". Also confirm no non-administrator can write to the truncated directories.

builtin_checks.title: No scheduled-task executable is writable by a non-administrator
builtin_checks.description: Each scheduled task's action executable is resolved and its ACL checked for write access granted to non-administrative principals.
builtin_checks.rationale: A task running as SYSTEM or an administrator executes whatever is at that path when it next fires. Overwriting it is code execution in that context, on the task's own schedule.
builtin_checks.remediation: Remove write access for non-administrative principals from the named executables, or repoint the task at a protected location.

builtin_checks.title: No directory on the system PATH is writable by a non-administrator
builtin_checks.description: Every directory on the machine PATH is checked for write access granted to Everyone, Users, Authenticated Users or Guests.
builtin_checks.rationale: Anything that resolves a command by name searches PATH in order. A writable directory early on it lets an unprivileged user place a binary that a privileged process then executes.
builtin_checks.remediation: Remove write access for non-administrative principals, or remove the directory from the machine PATH.

builtin_checks.title: No unattended-install answer file remains on disk
builtin_checks.description: Looks for Unattend.xml, unattend.xml and sysprep.inf in the locations Windows setup leaves them.
builtin_checks.rationale: These files routinely contain a local administrator password, in plain text or reversible base64, and are readable by any local user. They are one of the first things an attacker with a shell reads.
builtin_checks.remediation: Delete the named files. If the credential they contain is still in use anywhere, rotate it — assume it is known.

builtin_checks.title: Cached logon count is limited
builtin_checks.description: Reads CachedLogonsCount and reports a value above 4.
builtin_checks.rationale: Cached domain credentials can be extracted offline by anyone who obtains the machine or SYSTEM on it. Each cached logon is another account whose credential is recoverable from this host.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set CachedLogonsCount to 4 or fewer under Winlogon, or 0 where the host is always able to reach a domain controller.

builtin_checks.title: LSA runs as a protected process (RunAsPPL)
builtin_checks.description: Reads RunAsPPL under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa.
builtin_checks.rationale: Without LSA protection, credential material held in LSASS can be read by any process running as SYSTEM — which is exactly what the privilege-escalation conditions above grant.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set RunAsPPL to 1 and reboot. Confirm no driver or security agent in use requires unprotected access to LSASS first.

builtin_checks.title: PowerShell script-block logging is enabled
builtin_checks.description: Reads EnableScriptBlockLogging under the PowerShell policy key.
builtin_checks.rationale: This is not itself an escalation path, which is why it is Low. It is the reason one leaves no trace: without script-block logging there is no record of what was run, and an investigation into any of the conditions above has nothing to reconstruct.
builtin_checks.remediation: Enable 'Turn on PowerShell Script Block Logging' by policy, and forward the resulting events off the host.

builtin_checks.title: No directory on root's PATH is writable by a non-root user
builtin_checks.description: Each directory on root's PATH is checked for group- or world-writability, and for direct writability by the scanning account.
builtin_checks.rationale: Anything root runs by name resolves through PATH. A writable directory on it lets an unprivileged user place a binary that root then executes — an unconditional path to root that needs no other weakness.
builtin_checks.remediation: chmod go-w on the named directories, or remove them from root's PATH. A directory that must be writable does not belong on it.

builtin_checks.title: No sudo rule grants command execution without a password
builtin_checks.description: Parses /etc/sudoers and /etc/sudoers.d for rules carrying NOPASSWD, and reports the file and the rule.
builtin_checks.rationale: A NOPASSWD rule means anyone who obtains that account's shell — through a stolen key, a hijacked session, or a web shell — escalates with no credential at all. The password prompt is the last control between a compromised session and root.
builtin_checks.remediation: Remove NOPASSWD, or narrow it to the specific commands that need it. Where it exists for automation, prefer a dedicated account with a tightly scoped command list.

builtin_checks.title: No unexpected binary carries the SUID bit
builtin_checks.description: Every SUID binary on local filesystems is compared against the set a stock distribution ships. Only the difference is reported — a count of SUID binaries is not a finding.
builtin_checks.rationale: A SUID binary runs as its owner, usually root, whoever starts it. One outside the expected set is either a deliberate backdoor or a packaging mistake, and in both cases is a candidate for direct escalation.
builtin_checks.remediation: chmod u-s on the named binaries unless the SUID bit is required and understood. If it is required, record why.

builtin_checks.title: No world-writable directory is missing the sticky bit
builtin_checks.description: World-writable directories without the sticky bit. Directories that have it — /tmp and friends — are not reported.
builtin_checks.rationale: With the sticky bit a user may only delete their own files. Without it, any user can replace any other user's file in that directory, including one a privileged process later reads or executes.
builtin_checks.remediation: chmod +t on the named directories, or remove world-write where it is not needed.

builtin_checks.title: Root's PATH contains no relative or empty entry
builtin_checks.description: Checks root's PATH for empty entries — a leading, trailing or doubled colon — and for entries that are not absolute.
builtin_checks.rationale: An empty PATH entry means the current directory. A privileged process that changes into a directory an unprivileged user controls will then execute a binary from it by name.
builtin_checks.remediation: Remove empty and relative entries from root's PATH in the shell profile or the service unit that sets it.

builtin_checks.title: No systemd unit file is writable by a non-root user
builtin_checks.description: Service unit files under the systemd unit directories are checked for group- or world-writability.
builtin_checks.rationale: A writable unit file is root at the next daemon-reload or reboot: the ExecStart line is simply replaced. It is one of the most common real findings on a Linux estate and is invisible to every SUID, capability and sudo check.
builtin_checks.remediation: chmod go-w on the named unit files and confirm they are owned by root. Unit files should be 0644 root:root.

builtin_checks.title: No unexpected binary carries the SGID bit
builtin_checks.description: SGID binaries compared against the expected set, reporting only the difference.
builtin_checks.rationale: An SGID binary runs with its group's privileges. It is rated below SUID because group privilege is usually a smaller prize than root — but a group such as shadow or disk is not.
builtin_checks.remediation: chmod g-s on the named binaries unless the bit is required.

builtin_checks.title: No world-writable regular file outside pseudo-filesystems
builtin_checks.description: World-writable regular files on local filesystems.
builtin_checks.rationale: Any user can rewrite the contents. Where the file is a script, a configuration file or a library that something privileged reads, that is code execution in the reader's context.
builtin_checks.remediation: chmod o-w on the named files.

builtin_checks.title: Account database files are root-owned and correctly permissioned
builtin_checks.description: Ownership of /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /etc/group and /etc/gshadow, plus the modes of /etc/group and /etc/gshadow. The modes of passwd and shadow are asserted separately by the built-in file-permission checks and are not repeated here.
builtin_checks.rationale: These four files decide who may become whom. A non-root owner can rewrite them at will; a world-readable gshadow exposes group password hashes to offline cracking.
builtin_checks.remediation: chown root:root on all four. chmod 0644 /etc/group and chmod 0640 /etc/gshadow (0000 on distributions that expect it).

builtin_checks.title: No binary carries a privilege-granting file capability
builtin_checks.description: Every file capability on local filesystems, filtered to the ones that confer privilege — cap_setuid, cap_sys_admin, cap_dac_override and their neighbours. cap_net_bind_service is normal on a web server and is not reported.
builtin_checks.rationale: File capabilities are the modern replacement for the SUID bit and are invisible to every SUID check: a binary with cap_setuid+ep is a root shell and carries no SUID bit at all. A host can therefore pass every SUID check and still hand out root.
builtin_checks.remediation: setcap -r on the named binaries unless the capability is required and understood. Where it is required, prefer the narrowest capability that works.

builtin_checks.title: No file is owned by a user that does not exist
builtin_checks.description: Files whose owning uid has no entry in the password database.
builtin_checks.rationale: Usually the residue of a removed account. The risk is delayed rather than immediate: the next account assigned that uid silently inherits ownership of every one of these files.
builtin_checks.remediation: Reassign the named files to a valid owner, or remove them if the account they belonged to is gone for good.

builtin_checks.title: No file is owned by a group that does not exist
builtin_checks.description: Files whose owning gid has no entry in the group database.
builtin_checks.rationale: As with unowned files, the next group assigned that gid inherits access to all of them.
builtin_checks.remediation: Reassign the named files to a valid group, or remove them.

builtin_checks.title: No PostgreSQL login role has an empty password

collect.sql: SELECT rolname FROM pg_authid WHERE rolcanlogin AND rolpassword IS NULL

expect.description: no login role without a password

builtin_checks.description: Login roles whose password is unset. Such a role authenticates against any pg_hba rule that does not itself demand a password.
builtin_checks.rationale: A login role with no password is usable by anyone who can reach the port under a 'trust' rule, and cannot be used at all under a password rule — so it is either an open door or a broken account, and both warrant attention.
builtin_checks.remediation: ALTER ROLE <name> WITH PASSWORD '<value>'; for a role that should not log in, ALTER ROLE <name> WITH NOLOGIN.

builtin_checks.title: PostgreSQL stores passwords with SCRAM rather than MD5

collect.sql: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'password_encryption'

builtin_checks.description: The algorithm new and changed passwords are stored under.
builtin_checks.rationale: MD5 password verifiers are unsalted against the username only and are replayable: the stored hash is password-equivalent, so a read of pg_authid is enough to authenticate as the role.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set password_encryption = 'scram-sha-256', reload, then reset each role's password so the stored verifier is re-derived — changing the setting alone does not re-encode existing passwords.

builtin_checks.title: No PostgreSQL role still holds an MD5 password verifier

collect.sql: SELECT rolname FROM pg_authid WHERE rolcanlogin AND rolpassword LIKE 'md5%'

expect.description: no role on an MD5 verifier

builtin_checks.description: Roles whose stored verifier is still MD5 after the server was switched to SCRAM.
builtin_checks.rationale: Changing password_encryption does not re-encode existing passwords. A server reporting scram-sha-256 can still hold MD5 verifiers for every role created before the change, which is why this is checked separately from the setting.
builtin_checks.remediation: Reset the password for each listed role so the verifier is re-derived under SCRAM.

builtin_checks.title: PostgreSQL does not accept unauthenticated remote connections

collect.sql: SELECT type || ' ' || COALESCE(address, '') || ' ' || auth_method FROM pg_hba_file_rules WHERE auth_method IN ('trust', 'password') AND type <> 'local' AND COALESCE(address, '') NOT IN ('127.0.0.1', '::1', 'samehost', 'localhost')

expect.description: no remote trust or cleartext-password rule

builtin_checks.description: pg_hba.conf rules that accept a remote client with no password ('trust') or with a password sent in the clear ('password').
builtin_checks.rationale: A remote 'trust' rule makes every client that can reach the port a superuser without presenting anything. 'password' authenticates but transmits the secret unprotected unless the connection is already encrypted.
builtin_checks.remediation: Replace remote 'trust' and 'password' rules in pg_hba.conf with 'scram-sha-256', restrict the address range, and reload the server.

builtin_checks.title: PostgreSQL records authentication attempts

collect.sql: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'log_connections'

builtin_checks.description: Whether each connection attempt is written to the log.
builtin_checks.rationale: Without it there is no record of who authenticated, from where, or of a failed attempt — so neither a brute-force attempt nor the successful login that followed it leaves a trace.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set log_connections = on and reload the server.

builtin_checks.title: PostgreSQL superuser is limited to the bootstrap role

collect.sql: SELECT rolname FROM pg_roles WHERE rolsuper AND rolcanlogin AND rolname <> 'postgres'

builtin_checks.description: Roles that can log in and hold the superuser attribute, other than the bootstrap role the cluster was initialised with.
builtin_checks.rationale: A superuser bypasses every permission check, can read and write any file the server account can reach, and can execute code on the host through an untrusted procedural language. Each one is a full compromise of the instance and, usually, of its host.
builtin_checks.remediation: ALTER ROLE <name> NOSUPERUSER and grant the specific predefined role the account actually needs (pg_read_all_data, pg_monitor, pg_signal_backend).

builtin_checks.title: No PostgreSQL role holds server filesystem or program privileges

collect.sql: SELECT m.rolname || ' in ' || r.rolname FROM pg_auth_members am JOIN pg_roles r ON r.oid = am.roleid JOIN pg_roles m ON m.oid = am.member WHERE r.rolname IN ('pg_read_server_files', 'pg_write_server_files', 'pg_execute_server_program')

expect.description: no member of the filesystem roles

builtin_checks.description: Membership of pg_read_server_files, pg_write_server_files and pg_execute_server_program.
builtin_checks.rationale: These grant a non-superuser the ability to read any file the server account can read, write files it can write, and — for pg_execute_server_program — run commands on the host as the postgres operating-system user. Each is a route from a database login to the host.
builtin_checks.remediation: REVOKE the predefined role from the listed members and use COPY ... FROM STDIN through the client instead of server-side file access.

builtin_checks.title: PostgreSQL has no untrusted procedural language installed

collect.sql: SELECT lanname FROM pg_language WHERE lanispl AND NOT lanpltrusted

builtin_checks.description: Untrusted procedural languages (plpythonu, plperlu, plsh and similar) installed in the current database.
builtin_checks.rationale: An untrusted language runs without the sandbox a trusted one imposes, so a function written in it executes arbitrary code as the operating-system account the server runs under.
builtin_checks.remediation: DROP EXTENSION for any untrusted language that is not required. Where one is required, restrict CREATE FUNCTION on it and treat every function written in it as server-side code.

builtin_checks.title: PUBLIC cannot create objects in a PostgreSQL schema

collect.sql: SELECT nspname FROM pg_namespace WHERE has_schema_privilege('public', nspname, 'CREATE') AND nspname NOT LIKE 'pg\_%' AND nspname <> 'information_schema'

expect.description: no schema where PUBLIC may create

builtin_checks.description: Schemas in which the PUBLIC pseudo-role may create objects.
builtin_checks.rationale: Any role that can connect can then create functions and tables in such a schema. Where that schema is early on search_path, an attacker-created function can shadow a built-in and be executed by another user — the classic search_path hijack.
builtin_checks.remediation: REVOKE CREATE ON SCHEMA <name> FROM PUBLIC and grant it to the roles that genuinely need it. PostgreSQL 15 and later do this for the public schema by default.

builtin_checks.title: PUBLIC holds no privileges on user tables in PostgreSQL

collect.sql: SELECT table_schema || '.' || table_name || ' ' || privilege_type FROM information_schema.table_privileges WHERE grantee = 'PUBLIC' AND table_schema NOT IN ('pg_catalog', 'information_schema')

expect.description: no PUBLIC grant on user data

builtin_checks.description: Privileges granted to PUBLIC on tables outside the system catalogues.
builtin_checks.rationale: PUBLIC is every current and future role. A grant to it cannot be reasoned about from the role list, and it survives the creation of accounts nobody has thought about yet.
builtin_checks.remediation: REVOKE the listed privileges FROM PUBLIC and grant them to named roles.

builtin_checks.title: PostgreSQL offers TLS to clients

collect.sql: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'ssl'

builtin_checks.description: Whether the server was built and configured to accept TLS.
builtin_checks.rationale: With ssl off, every session — including the authentication exchange and every row returned — crosses the network in the clear, and no client setting can change that.
builtin_checks.remediation: Install a server certificate and key, set ssl = on, and restart the server.

builtin_checks.title: PostgreSQL requires TLS for remote connections

collect.sql: SELECT type || ' ' || COALESCE(address, '') || ' ' || auth_method FROM pg_hba_file_rules WHERE type IN ('host', 'hostnossl') AND auth_method <> 'reject' AND COALESCE(address, '') NOT IN ('127.0.0.1', '::1', 'samehost', 'localhost')

builtin_checks.description: pg_hba.conf rules that admit a remote client over an unencrypted connection. 'host' matches both encrypted and unencrypted; only 'hostssl' requires TLS.
builtin_checks.rationale: Enabling TLS makes it available, not mandatory. While a 'host' rule matches a remote address, a client that simply does not ask for TLS is still admitted, and the server-side setting gives no indication that this is happening.
builtin_checks.remediation: Change remote 'host' rules to 'hostssl' in pg_hba.conf, keeping loopback entries as they are, and reload the server.

builtin_checks.title: PostgreSQL refuses TLS below 1.2

collect.sql: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'ssl_min_protocol_version'

builtin_checks.description: The lowest TLS protocol version the server will negotiate.
builtin_checks.rationale: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are deprecated by RFC 8996 and permit cipher suites with known weaknesses. A server that still offers them will negotiate down for any client that asks.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set ssl_min_protocol_version = 'TLSv1.2' and reload.

builtin_checks.title: PostgreSQL logs schema and privilege changes

collect.sql: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'log_statement'

builtin_checks.description: Which statement classes are written to the log. 'ddl' captures CREATE, ALTER, DROP, GRANT and REVOKE.
builtin_checks.rationale: At 'none' there is no record that a table was dropped or a privilege granted. An investigation into how an account acquired a right has nothing to read.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set log_statement = 'ddl' as a minimum and reload. 'mod' and 'all' capture more at a proportionate cost in log volume.

builtin_checks.title: PostgreSQL records session end and duration

collect.sql: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'log_disconnections'

builtin_checks.description: Whether session termination and duration are logged, which pairs with log_connections to bound a session in time.
builtin_checks.rationale: A connection record without a matching disconnection record cannot establish how long an account held a session, which is what correlating database activity with other evidence needs.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set log_disconnections = on and reload the server.

builtin_checks.title: PostgreSQL rotates its log files

collect.sql: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'log_rotation_age'

builtin_checks.description: The age at which the server starts a new log file.
builtin_checks.rationale: With rotation disabled the server writes to one file indefinitely. That file is eventually too large to read, and nothing bounds the disk it consumes.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set log_rotation_age (minutes) and log_rotation_size, and keep logging_collector on so the server manages the files.

builtin_checks.title: PostgreSQL does not listen on every interface

collect.sql: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'listen_addresses'

expect.description: a named address, not a wildcard

builtin_checks.description: The interfaces the postmaster binds to.
builtin_checks.rationale: Binding to every interface exposes the instance on networks it has no reason to be reachable from — a management VLAN, a second NIC, a container network — where pg_hba is the only remaining control.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set listen_addresses to the specific addresses clients use and restart. This is a restart-only setting.

builtin_checks.title: PostgreSQL is a release still receiving fixes

collect.sql: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'server_version_num'

builtin_checks.description: The running major version, against the oldest release under the PostgreSQL five-year support policy.
builtin_checks.rationale: An out-of-support release receives no fixes for vulnerabilities found after its end-of-life date, so its CVE exposure only grows and no patch will ever close it.
builtin_checks.remediation: Plan a major-version upgrade. Check the current support window at https://www.postgresql.org/support/versioning/ — this rule's boundary was set in August 2026 and moves each November.

builtin_checks.title: PostgreSQL does not permit direct system catalogue modification

collect.sql: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'allow_system_table_mods'

builtin_checks.description: Whether the structure of system catalogues may be altered directly.
builtin_checks.rationale: With this on, a superuser can corrupt the catalogue in ways the server cannot recover from, and can alter the very tables that record who holds which privilege.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set allow_system_table_mods = off and restart the server.

builtin_checks.title: PostgreSQL reserves connection slots for administrators

collect.sql: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'superuser_reserved_connections'

builtin_checks.description: Connection slots held back from ordinary roles so an administrator can still connect.
builtin_checks.rationale: Without a reserve, an application that exhausts max_connections locks administrators out of the instance that needs fixing — the connection storm and the inability to diagnose it arrive together.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set superuser_reserved_connections to at least 3 and restart.

builtin_checks.title: PostgreSQL carries no sample database

collect.sql: SELECT datname FROM pg_database WHERE datname IN ('pagila', 'dellstore', 'dellstore2', 'sakila', 'northwind', 'adventureworks', 'chinook', 'employees')

builtin_checks.description: Well-known demonstration databases left on a production instance.
builtin_checks.rationale: Sample databases ship with permissive grants and predictable object names, and their presence usually means the instance was built from a tutorial rather than from a hardened baseline.
builtin_checks.remediation: DROP DATABASE for any sample database not in use.

builtin_checks.title: No MySQL account has an empty password

collect.sql: SELECT CONCAT(user, '@', host) FROM mysql.user WHERE authentication_string = '' AND plugin NOT IN ('auth_socket', 'unix_socket', 'mysql_no_login')

builtin_checks.description: Accounts with no stored password. Accounts authenticating through the operating-system socket or explicitly barred from logging in are excluded, because for those an empty password column is normal and correct.
builtin_checks.rationale: An account with no password is usable by anyone who can reach the port, with whatever privileges it holds and from whatever hosts its host column permits.
builtin_checks.remediation: ALTER USER '<user>'@'<host>' IDENTIFIED BY '<password>'; or DROP USER for an account that is not needed.

builtin_checks.title: MySQL has no anonymous account

collect.sql: SELECT CONCAT('anonymous@', host) FROM mysql.user WHERE user = ''

builtin_checks.description: Accounts with an empty user name, which MySQL matches for any user name a client presents.
builtin_checks.rationale: An anonymous account lets a client connect under a name that was never created. It also changes how MySQL matches every other account, because the most specific host wins — so an anonymous entry for a host can take precedence over a named account and silently deny the privileges that account was granted.
builtin_checks.remediation: DROP USER ''@'<host>'; for each anonymous entry.

builtin_checks.title: No MySQL account uses a legacy authentication plugin

collect.sql: SELECT CONCAT(user, '@', host, ' uses ', plugin) FROM mysql.user WHERE plugin IN ('mysql_native_password', 'mysql_old_password')

expect.description: no account on a legacy plugin

builtin_checks.description: Accounts still authenticating with mysql_native_password or the pre-4.1 mysql_old_password.
builtin_checks.rationale: Both store a bare SHA-1 of the password with no salt and no iteration, so the stored value is password-equivalent and identical passwords are visibly identical across accounts. mysql_native_password is deprecated as of MySQL 8.0.34.
builtin_checks.remediation: ALTER USER '<user>'@'<host>' IDENTIFIED WITH caching_sha2_password BY '<password>'; after confirming every client library supports it.

builtin_checks.title: MySQL root is restricted to the local host

collect.sql: SELECT CONCAT(user, '@', host) FROM mysql.user WHERE user = 'root' AND host NOT IN ('localhost', '127.0.0.1', '::1')

builtin_checks.description: root accounts whose host column admits connections from beyond the local machine.
builtin_checks.rationale: root holds every privilege including FILE and SUPER. A root entry for '%' means one guessed or leaked password is a full compromise of the instance from anywhere that can reach the port, with no second factor and no network restriction in the way.
builtin_checks.remediation: DROP USER 'root'@'%'; and administer through a named account restricted to the hosts that need it, or over a local socket.

builtin_checks.title: MySQL enforces a password policy

collect.sql: SELECT plugin_name AS item FROM information_schema.plugins WHERE plugin_name LIKE 'validate_password%' AND plugin_status = 'ACTIVE' UNION ALL SELECT component_urn AS item FROM mysql.component WHERE component_urn LIKE '%validate_password%'

expect.description: the password plugin or component is active

builtin_checks.description: Whether the validate_password component or plugin is installed and active.
builtin_checks.rationale: Without it the server accepts any password an administrator types, including a single character, and nothing at the database layer enforces the organisation's policy.
builtin_checks.remediation: INSTALL COMPONENT 'file://component_validate_password'; then set validate_password.length and validate_password.policy to match the organisation's standard.

builtin_checks.title: No ordinary MySQL account holds administrative privileges

collect.sql: SELECT CONCAT(grantee, ' holds ', privilege_type) FROM information_schema.user_privileges WHERE privilege_type IN ('SUPER', 'SHUTDOWN', 'PROCESS') AND grantee NOT LIKE '''root''@%' AND grantee NOT LIKE '''mysql.%'

builtin_checks.description: Accounts other than root and MySQL's own internal accounts holding SUPER, SHUTDOWN or PROCESS.
builtin_checks.rationale: SUPER overrides read_only, permits changing global variables, and lets an account kill other sessions. PROCESS exposes the statements every other session is running, which routinely include credentials passed as literals.
builtin_checks.remediation: REVOKE SUPER, SHUTDOWN, PROCESS ON *.* FROM '<user>'@'<host>'; and grant the specific dynamic privilege the account needs (BINLOG_ADMIN, SYSTEM_VARIABLES_ADMIN).

builtin_checks.title: No ordinary MySQL account holds the FILE privilege

collect.sql: SELECT CONCAT(user, '@', host) FROM mysql.user WHERE File_priv = 'Y' AND user <> 'root' AND user NOT LIKE 'mysql.%'

builtin_checks.description: Accounts other than root holding FILE, which permits reading and writing files on the server host through SQL.
builtin_checks.rationale: FILE turns a database login into a filesystem read of anything the mysqld account can read — /etc/passwd, application configuration, private keys — and a write of anything it can write, which includes locations that lead to code execution.
builtin_checks.remediation: REVOKE FILE ON *.* FROM '<user>'@'<host>'; and keep secure_file_priv pointed at a dedicated directory.

builtin_checks.title: MySQL confines server-side file access to one directory

collect.sql: SELECT COALESCE(@@GLOBAL.secure_file_priv, 'DISABLED')

expect.description: a directory, or NULL to disable file access entirely

builtin_checks.description: The directory LOAD DATA and SELECT ... INTO OUTFILE are confined to. An empty value means no confinement at all.
builtin_checks.rationale: With secure_file_priv empty, any account holding FILE can read and write anywhere the server process can. The privilege and this setting are two halves of one control, which is why both are checked.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set secure_file_priv to a dedicated directory in the server configuration and restart, or set it to NULL to disable server-side file access entirely.

builtin_checks.title: MySQL offers TLS to clients

collect.sql: SELECT @@GLOBAL.have_ssl

builtin_checks.description: Whether the server has a usable certificate and key.
builtin_checks.rationale: Without TLS the authentication exchange and every row returned cross the network in the clear.
builtin_checks.remediation: Provide ssl_cert, ssl_key and ssl_ca in the server configuration and restart. MySQL 8 generates a self-signed set at first start if none is supplied.

builtin_checks.title: MySQL requires encrypted client connections

collect.sql: SELECT @@GLOBAL.require_secure_transport

builtin_checks.description: Whether the server refuses connections that are neither encrypted nor over a local socket.
builtin_checks.rationale: Offering TLS is not requiring it. With this off a client that simply does not ask for encryption is still accepted, and nothing on the server indicates that it happened.
builtin_checks.remediation: SET PERSIST require_secure_transport = ON; after confirming every client connects over TLS or a local socket.

builtin_checks.title: MySQL offers no TLS version below 1.2

collect.sql: SELECT @@GLOBAL.tls_version

expect.description: no TLSv1 or TLSv1.1 in the offered list

builtin_checks.description: The TLS protocol versions the server will negotiate.
builtin_checks.rationale: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are deprecated by RFC 8996. While they remain in the offered list the server will negotiate down for any client that asks for them.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set tls_version='TLSv1.2,TLSv1.3' and restart the server.

builtin_checks.title: MySQL does not permit LOAD DATA LOCAL

collect.sql: SELECT @@GLOBAL.local_infile

builtin_checks.description: Whether the server accepts LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE, which reads a file from the *client* rather than the server.
builtin_checks.rationale: The server tells the client which file to send. A malicious or compromised server can therefore request any file the client process can read — the 'rogue MySQL server' technique — so this is a risk to everything that connects, not only to the server.
builtin_checks.remediation: SET PERSIST local_infile = OFF;

builtin_checks.title: MySQL does not listen on every interface

collect.sql: SELECT @@GLOBAL.bind_address

expect.description: a named address, not a wildcard

builtin_checks.description: The addresses mysqld binds its TCP listener to.
builtin_checks.rationale: Binding to every interface exposes the instance on networks it has no reason to be reachable from, leaving the account host column as the only remaining control.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set bind_address to the specific addresses clients use and restart the server.

builtin_checks.title: MySQL is a release still receiving fixes

collect.sql: SELECT @@GLOBAL.version

builtin_checks.description: The running server version against Oracle's support policy.
builtin_checks.rationale: An out-of-support release receives no fixes for vulnerabilities found after its end date, so its exposure only grows.
builtin_checks.remediation: Plan an upgrade. Check the current support window at https://endoflife.date/mysql — this rule's boundary was set in August 2026.

builtin_checks.title: MySQL carries no sample schema

collect.sql: SELECT schema_name FROM information_schema.schemata WHERE schema_name IN ('test', 'world', 'world_x', 'sakila', 'employees', 'menagerie')

builtin_checks.description: Demonstration schemas left on a production instance.
builtin_checks.rationale: The historical 'test' schema was writable by any account that could connect. The others ship with predictable object names and usually indicate the instance was built from a tutorial rather than a hardened baseline.
builtin_checks.remediation: DROP DATABASE for any sample schema not in use.

builtin_checks.title: No SQL Server login has a blank password

collect.sql: SELECT name FROM sys.sql_logins WHERE PWDCOMPARE('', password_hash) = 1 AND is_disabled = 0

expect.description: no login with a blank password

builtin_checks.description: Enabled SQL logins whose password is the empty string, tested with PWDCOMPARE against the stored hash.
builtin_checks.rationale: A blank password on an enabled login is usable by anyone who can reach the instance. PWDCOMPARE tests the stored verifier directly, so this establishes the fact rather than inferring it from policy settings.
builtin_checks.remediation: ALTER LOGIN [<name>] WITH PASSWORD = '<value>'; or DISABLE the login if it is not in use.

builtin_checks.title: No SQL Server login uses its own name as the password

collect.sql: SELECT name FROM sys.sql_logins WHERE PWDCOMPARE(name, password_hash) = 1 AND is_disabled = 0

expect.description: no login whose password is its name

builtin_checks.description: Enabled logins whose password is identical to the login name.
builtin_checks.rationale: It is the first guess any credential-stuffing attempt makes, and PWDCOMPARE can establish it without attempting a single login — so the check produces no failed-authentication events and cannot lock an account out.
builtin_checks.remediation: ALTER LOGIN [<name>] WITH PASSWORD = '<value>';

builtin_checks.title: SQL Server logins are subject to the password policy

collect.sql: SELECT name FROM sys.sql_logins WHERE is_policy_checked = 0 AND is_disabled = 0

expect.description: every enabled login has CHECK_POLICY on

builtin_checks.description: Enabled SQL logins created or altered with CHECK_POLICY = OFF.
builtin_checks.rationale: With CHECK_POLICY off, the login is exempt from the host's password complexity and lockout policy, so it accepts a password the organisation's standard would refuse and survives unlimited guessing.
builtin_checks.remediation: ALTER LOGIN [<name>] WITH CHECK_POLICY = ON; and reset the password, since the existing one was never tested against the policy.

builtin_checks.title: The SQL Server sa login is disabled

collect.sql: SELECT name FROM sys.sql_logins WHERE sid = 0x01 AND is_disabled = 0

builtin_checks.description: Whether the built-in sa login is enabled. Identified by its fixed SID rather than by name, so renaming it does not hide it.
builtin_checks.rationale: sa is a sysadmin whose name is known to every attacker and which no audit trail can attribute to a person. It is the single most targeted account name in SQL Server credential attacks.
builtin_checks.remediation: ALTER LOGIN [sa] DISABLE; after confirming no application uses it, and administer through named accounts.

builtin_checks.title: SQL Server sysadmin membership is limited

collect.sql: SELECT p.name FROM sys.server_role_members m JOIN sys.server_principals r ON r.principal_id = m.role_principal_id JOIN sys.server_principals p ON p.principal_id = m.member_principal_id WHERE r.name = 'sysadmin' AND p.name <> 'sa' AND p.name NOT LIKE 'NT AUTHORITY\%' AND p.name NOT LIKE 'NT SERVICE\%' AND p.name NOT LIKE 'BUILTIN\%'

expect.description: no sysadmin beyond sa and service accounts

builtin_checks.description: Members of the sysadmin server role, excluding sa and the principals SQL Server provisions for its own services.
builtin_checks.rationale: sysadmin bypasses every permission check in the instance and can reach the host through xp_cmdshell, CLR assemblies or a startup procedure. Membership is effectively administrator on the server, not merely on the database.
builtin_checks.remediation: ALTER SERVER ROLE sysadmin DROP MEMBER [<name>]; and grant the narrower fixed role or permission the account needs.

builtin_checks.title: SQL Server public role holds no granted server permission

collect.sql: SELECT pe.permission_name FROM sys.server_permissions pe JOIN sys.server_principals pr ON pr.principal_id = pe.grantee_principal_id WHERE pr.name = 'public' AND pe.state_desc = 'GRANT' AND pe.permission_name NOT LIKE 'CONNECT%' AND pe.permission_name <> 'VIEW ANY DATABASE'

builtin_checks.description: Server-level permissions granted to the public role beyond the defaults every instance carries.
builtin_checks.rationale: Every login is a member of public and cannot be removed from it, so a grant there reaches accounts nobody has created yet and cannot be reasoned about from the login list.
builtin_checks.remediation: REVOKE <permission> FROM public; and grant it to the specific logins or roles that need it.

builtin_checks.title: SQL Server bulk filesystem access is not granted broadly

collect.sql: SELECT pr.name FROM sys.server_permissions pe JOIN sys.server_principals pr ON pr.principal_id = pe.grantee_principal_id WHERE pe.permission_name = 'ADMINISTER BULK OPERATIONS' AND pe.state_desc = 'GRANT' AND pr.name <> 'sa'

builtin_checks.description: Principals granted ADMINISTER BULK OPERATIONS, which permits BULK INSERT and OPENROWSET(BULK …).
builtin_checks.rationale: The permission reads any file the SQL Server service account can read, returned as a result set — configuration files, private keys, anything on a share the service account reaches. It is a filesystem read wearing a database permission.
builtin_checks.remediation: REVOKE ADMINISTER BULK OPERATIONS FROM [<name>]; and stage bulk loads through a controlled directory instead.

builtin_checks.title: SQL Server command-execution features are disabled

collect.sql: SELECT name FROM sys.configurations WHERE name IN ('xp_cmdshell', 'Ole Automation Procedures', 'clr enabled', 'Ad Hoc Distributed Queries', 'cross db ownership chaining', 'scan for startup procs') AND value_in_use <> 0

expect.description: none of the listed options is enabled

builtin_checks.description: Server options that let SQL execute code outside the database engine: xp_cmdshell, OLE Automation, CLR, Ad Hoc Distributed Queries, cross-database ownership chaining and startup procedure scanning.
builtin_checks.rationale: xp_cmdshell runs operating-system commands as the service account, and OLE Automation and CLR reach the host the same way by other routes. Each turns a SQL injection flaw in any application using this instance into code execution on the server.
builtin_checks.remediation: sp_configure the named option to 0 followed by RECONFIGURE. Where a feature is genuinely required, restrict who may invoke it and record the exception.

builtin_checks.title: SQL Server encrypts client connections

collect.sql: SELECT CAST(encrypt_option AS VARCHAR(10)) FROM sys.dm_exec_connections WHERE session_id = @@SPID

builtin_checks.description: Whether this scanner's own session is encrypted, having requested encryption.
builtin_checks.rationale: The scanner requests encryption on connection. A session that is nonetheless unencrypted establishes that the instance accepts plaintext, so the authentication exchange and every result set cross the network in the clear for any client that does not ask.
builtin_checks.remediation: Install a certificate and set ForceEncryption in SQL Server Configuration Manager, then restart the service.

builtin_checks.title: SQL Server has a running audit

collect.sql: SELECT name FROM sys.dm_server_audit_status WHERE status_desc = 'STARTED'

expect.description: at least one audit is started

builtin_checks.description: Server audit objects that are defined and running.
builtin_checks.rationale: SQL Server Audit is the only facility that records privileged activity in a form an investigation can rely on. Without one running, no record exists of who granted a permission, read a table or enabled xp_cmdshell.
builtin_checks.remediation: CREATE SERVER AUDIT with a file or event-log target, then ALTER SERVER AUDIT ... WITH (STATE = ON).

builtin_checks.title: SQL Server audit has an enabled specification

collect.sql: SELECT name FROM sys.server_audit_specifications WHERE is_state_enabled = 1

builtin_checks.description: Server audit specifications that are enabled. A specification is what names the action groups an audit records.
builtin_checks.rationale: A running audit with no enabled specification records nothing. This is checked separately from the audit itself because the two fail independently and the combination looks configured from a distance — the audit object exists, the log file is created, and it stays empty.
builtin_checks.remediation: CREATE SERVER AUDIT SPECIFICATION covering at least SUCCESSFUL_LOGIN_GROUP, FAILED_LOGIN_GROUP, SERVER_ROLE_MEMBER_CHANGE_GROUP and SERVER_PERMISSION_CHANGE_GROUP, then set STATE = ON.

builtin_checks.title: SQL Server is a release still receiving fixes

collect.sql: SELECT CAST(PARSENAME(CAST(SERVERPROPERTY('ProductVersion') AS VARCHAR(64)), 4) AS INT)

builtin_checks.description: The instance's major version against Microsoft's support lifecycle.
builtin_checks.rationale: An instance past Extended Support receives no security updates, so its exposure only grows and no patch will ever close it.
builtin_checks.remediation: Plan an upgrade. Check the current lifecycle at https://learn.microsoft.com/lifecycle/products/ — this rule's boundary was set in August 2026.

builtin_checks.title: SQL Server carries no sample database

collect.sql: SELECT name FROM sys.databases WHERE name IN ('AdventureWorks', 'AdventureWorksDW', 'AdventureWorks2019', 'AdventureWorks2022', 'Northwind', 'pubs', 'WideWorldImporters', 'WideWorldImportersDW')

builtin_checks.description: Microsoft sample databases attached to the instance.
builtin_checks.rationale: Sample databases ship with permissive object-level grants and predictable names, and their presence on a production instance usually indicates it was built from a walkthrough rather than from a hardened baseline.
builtin_checks.remediation: DROP DATABASE for any sample database not in use.

builtin_checks.title: nginx does not advertise its version
builtin_checks.description: Whether nginx includes its version in error pages and the Server header. Unset, nginx defaults to 'on'.
builtin_checks.rationale: The exact patch version tells an attacker which published vulnerabilities apply before they probe for any of them, turning a scan of the estate into a target list.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set 'server_tokens off;' in the http block and reload.

builtin_checks.title: nginx does not expose the stub_status endpoint
builtin_checks.description: Locations serving the stub_status module, which reports active connections and request counters.
builtin_checks.rationale: stub_status is unauthenticated by default and discloses live traffic volumes and connection state — useful for timing an attack and for confirming that one is working.
builtin_checks.remediation: Remove the stub_status location, or restrict it with 'allow'/'deny' to the monitoring host only.

builtin_checks.title: nginx worker processes do not run as root
builtin_checks.description: The account nginx drops to for its worker processes. Unset, nginx uses the user its build specifies, commonly 'nobody'.
builtin_checks.rationale: Workers handle untrusted input. A memory-safety flaw in a worker running as root is a full host compromise rather than a compromise of the web content.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set 'user nginx;' (or another unprivileged account) and reload.

builtin_checks.title: nginx offers no TLS version below 1.2
builtin_checks.description: The TLS versions nginx will negotiate. Unset, nginx uses its build default, which for 1.27 is TLSv1 TLSv1.1 TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3.
builtin_checks.rationale: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are deprecated by RFC 8996 and permit cipher suites with known weaknesses. While they remain in the list the server negotiates down for any client that asks.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set 'ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;' and reload.

builtin_checks.title: nginx excludes null, export and anonymous cipher suites

expect.description: no NULL, EXPORT, LOW, RC4, DES or MD5 suites

builtin_checks.description: The cipher suite list offered to clients. Unset, nginx uses OpenSSL's HIGH:!aNULL:!MD5 default.
builtin_checks.rationale: An anonymous or NULL suite provides no authentication or no encryption at all while still completing a handshake, so the connection looks protected in the client and is not.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set an explicit modern list, for example 'ssl_ciphers ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:...;' with '!aNULL:!MD5:!EXPORT' appended.

builtin_checks.title: nginx enforces its own cipher preference order
builtin_checks.description: Whether the server's cipher order wins over the client's. Unset, nginx defaults to 'off' and the client chooses.
builtin_checks.rationale: With the client choosing, a downgrade-inclined or simply outdated client selects the weakest suite both sides share, and the server's carefully ordered list has no effect. Note this applies to TLS 1.2 and below; TLS 1.3 removes the negotiation entirely.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set 'ssl_prefer_server_ciphers on;' and reload.

builtin_checks.title: nginx records access to served content
builtin_checks.description: The http-level access log. 'off' disables it; unset, nginx logs to its compiled-in default path.
builtin_checks.rationale: Without an access log there is no record of what was requested or by whom, so neither an investigation nor an abuse report has anything to work from.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set 'access_log /var/log/nginx/access.log main;' in the http block, or a destination your log pipeline collects.

builtin_checks.title: nginx records errors at a usable level

expect.description: notice, info, warn or error — not only the fatal levels

builtin_checks.description: The main error log and its level. Unset, nginx logs to its compiled-in default at 'error'.
builtin_checks.rationale: At 'crit' and above the log records only what has already broken. Rejected requests, failed TLS handshakes and permission problems — the entries an investigation actually reads — are all below that threshold.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set 'error_log /var/log/nginx/error.log warn;' and reload.

builtin_checks.title: nginx bounds the size of a request body
builtin_checks.description: The largest request body nginx accepts. '0' disables the limit entirely; unset, nginx defaults to 1m.
builtin_checks.rationale: An unbounded body lets one client consume disk in the temp directory and memory in the worker, so a single request becomes a denial-of-service primitive that needs no volume behind it.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set 'client_max_body_size' to the largest upload the application genuinely needs.

builtin_checks.title: nginx closes idle keep-alive connections
builtin_checks.description: How long an idle keep-alive connection is held open. Unset, nginx defaults to 75s.
builtin_checks.rationale: Idle connections occupy worker slots. Without a timeout a client that opens connections and never uses them exhausts the connection pool at negligible cost to itself — the slowloris shape.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set 'keepalive_timeout 65;' or lower in the http block.

builtin_checks.title: Apache does not advertise its version and modules
builtin_checks.description: What Apache puts in the Server header. Unset, httpd 2.4 defaults to 'Full', which names the version and every loaded module.
builtin_checks.rationale: The module list is more useful to an attacker than the version: it says which attack surface is actually compiled in and loaded, before a single request has been sent to test for it.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set 'ServerTokens Prod' at the top level and restart.

builtin_checks.title: Apache does not expose server-status or server-info
builtin_checks.description: Locations configured with the server-status or server-info handlers.
builtin_checks.rationale: server-status lists every in-flight request with its client address and URL, and server-info dumps the full configuration including paths and module settings. Both are routinely left reachable after a debugging session.
builtin_checks.remediation: Remove the SetHandler block, or confine it with 'Require ip <management network>'.

builtin_checks.title: Apache does not run its workers as root
builtin_checks.description: The account child processes drop to. On Windows this directive does not apply, which is why the check defers rather than failing when it is absent.
builtin_checks.rationale: Child processes parse untrusted request data. One running as root turns a parsing flaw into host compromise rather than into compromise of the served content.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set 'User www-data' (or the distribution's service account) and restart. The parent still starts as root to bind port 80.

builtin_checks.title: Apache does not honour .htaccess overrides

expect.description: None or a named directive group, never All

builtin_checks.description: Whether per-directory .htaccess files may override the server configuration, read across every <Directory> container. Unset, httpd 2.4 defaults to None.
builtin_checks.rationale: 'AllowOverride All' lets anyone who can write a file into the document root change the server's authentication, rewriting and handler configuration. An upload flaw becomes a configuration change, and Apache re-reads it on the next request.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set 'AllowOverride None' and move the needed directives into the server configuration, where they are version-controlled.

builtin_checks.title: Apache logs at a level that records rejected requests
builtin_checks.description: The error log verbosity. Unset, httpd defaults to 'warn'.
builtin_checks.rationale: At 'error' and above the log records failures of the server, not refusals by it. Authorisation denials and rejected requests — the entries that show an attack in progress — are logged at 'warn'.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set 'LogLevel warn' and restart.

builtin_checks.title: Apache records access to served content
builtin_checks.description: Access log destinations configured anywhere in the tree. This counts matches, so it never reports an absent reading and the absence policy below is unreachable; it is declared because ConfigCheck requires a choice.
builtin_checks.rationale: Without an access log there is no record of what was requested or from where, so neither an investigation nor an abuse report has anything to work from.
builtin_checks.remediation: Add 'CustomLog logs/access_log combined' at the server level or in each virtual host.

builtin_checks.title: Apache records errors to a defined destination
builtin_checks.description: The error log destination. This counts matches, so it never reports an absent reading and the absence policy below is unreachable; it is declared because ConfigCheck requires a choice.
builtin_checks.rationale: The error log is where a failed authorisation, a module failure and a malformed request all surface. Unset, output goes wherever the service manager sends stderr, which may be nowhere.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set 'ErrorLog logs/error_log' or a destination you collect.

builtin_checks.title: Apache bounds how long a request may take
builtin_checks.description: Seconds Apache waits for a request to complete. Unset, httpd 2.4 defaults to 60.
builtin_checks.rationale: A long timeout is what makes a slow-request attack cheap: each connection occupies a worker for the whole interval while costing the client nothing but a socket.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set 'Timeout 60' and consider mod_reqtimeout as well.

builtin_checks.title: Tomcat does not use the default shutdown command
builtin_checks.description: The word that stops the server when sent to the shutdown port. Tomcat ships the literal string 'SHUTDOWN'. Unset, the attribute is required by the schema, so its absence means the file could not be read as expected rather than a default.
builtin_checks.rationale: Anyone who can reach the shutdown port and send this word stops the server. No authentication is involved and none is possible — the word is the only secret, and by default it is published in every copy of Tomcat's documentation.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set a long random 'shutdown' value on <Server>, or disable the port entirely with port="-1".

builtin_checks.title: Tomcat's shutdown port is disabled
builtin_checks.description: The <Server> shutdown port. '-1' disables the listener entirely; Tomcat ships 8005. Unset, the attribute is required by the schema, so its absence means the file could not be read as expected rather than a default.
builtin_checks.rationale: The listener accepts a plain-text word on a local socket and stops the server. Where the shutdown command has been changed the risk is lower, but a listener that cannot be reached at all is the only state with no residual risk.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set port="-1" on <Server> and stop Tomcat through the service manager instead.

builtin_checks.title: Tomcat defines no accounts in tomcat-users.xml
builtin_checks.description: Accounts defined in the file-based realm. The official image ships this file with every user commented out.
builtin_checks.rationale: The file realm stores passwords in cleartext by default and is what the manager application authenticates against. Accounts here are frequently left from a tutorial, with the credentials that tutorial published.
builtin_checks.remediation: Remove the <user> entries and authenticate the manager application against the organisation's directory, or delete the manager application if it is not used.

builtin_checks.title: Tomcat records access to deployed applications
builtin_checks.description: AccessLogValve entries anywhere in server.xml. This counts matches, so it never reports an absent reading and the absence policy below is unreachable; it is declared because ConfigCheck requires a choice.
builtin_checks.rationale: Tomcat writes no request log at all without this valve. The catalina log records the server's own lifecycle, not what was requested, so an investigation into an application compromise has nothing to read.
builtin_checks.remediation: Add an AccessLogValve to the <Host>, with a pattern that includes the client address and the request line.

builtin_checks.title: Tomcat connectors do not advertise the product

expect.description: a neutral Server header, or none

builtin_checks.description: The 'server' attribute on each <Connector>. Unset, Tomcat sends 'Apache-Coyote/1.1'.
builtin_checks.rationale: Naming the product and its connector tells an attacker which published vulnerabilities to try before probing for any of them.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set server="" or a neutral value on each <Connector>. Note this is obscurity, not a control, and does not replace patching.

builtin_checks.title: Tomcat does not deploy the manager application
builtin_checks.description: Whether Tomcat's bundled 'manager' application is deployed. The official image moves the bundled applications to webapps.dist/, so a stock container has none of them deployed.
builtin_checks.rationale: The manager application deploys and undeploys web applications. An authenticated session with it is remote code execution by design, which is why it is the first thing every Tomcat credential-guessing tool tries.
builtin_checks.remediation: Delete /usr/local/tomcat/webapps/manager if the application is not required. Where it is, restrict it by address and authenticate it against the organisation's directory.

builtin_checks.title: Tomcat does not deploy the host-manager application
builtin_checks.description: Whether Tomcat's bundled 'host-manager' application is deployed. The official image moves the bundled applications to webapps.dist/, so a stock container has none of them deployed.
builtin_checks.rationale: host-manager creates and removes virtual hosts, so it controls which applications the server will serve at all. Like manager, an authenticated session with it is equivalent to control of the server.
builtin_checks.remediation: Delete /usr/local/tomcat/webapps/host-manager if the application is not required. Where it is, restrict it by address and authenticate it against the organisation's directory.

builtin_checks.title: Tomcat does not deploy the examples application
builtin_checks.description: Whether Tomcat's bundled 'examples' application is deployed. The official image moves the bundled applications to webapps.dist/, so a stock container has none of them deployed.
builtin_checks.rationale: The examples application has historically shipped servlets that echo request data and expose session contents, and it exists only to demonstrate the product. On a production server it is attack surface with no purpose.
builtin_checks.remediation: Delete /usr/local/tomcat/webapps/examples if the application is not required. Where it is, restrict it by address and authenticate it against the organisation's directory.

builtin_checks.title: Tomcat does not deploy the documentation application
builtin_checks.description: Whether Tomcat's bundled 'docs' application is deployed. The official image moves the bundled applications to webapps.dist/, so a stock container has none of them deployed.
builtin_checks.rationale: The bundled documentation states the exact Tomcat version it was shipped with, which identifies the build to anyone who can reach it without any probing.
builtin_checks.remediation: Delete /usr/local/tomcat/webapps/docs if the application is not required. Where it is, restrict it by address and authenticate it against the organisation's directory.

builtin_checks.title: The Docker daemon does not listen on a TCP socket
builtin_checks.description: The sockets dockerd binds. Unset, it listens only on /var/run/docker.sock.
builtin_checks.rationale: The Docker API is root-equivalent by design: anyone who can reach it can start a privileged container that mounts the host filesystem. Exposed over TCP without mutual TLS it is an unauthenticated root shell on the host, reachable from anywhere the port is.
builtin_checks.remediation: Remove the tcp:// entry from 'hosts'. Where remote access is genuinely needed, use an SSH context rather than a TCP socket.

builtin_checks.title: The Docker daemon requires TLS client certificates
builtin_checks.description: Whether dockerd verifies client certificates. Unset, Docker defaults to false. Only meaningful alongside a TCP socket; on a unix-socket-only daemon it is not used, which is why an absent reading defers rather than failing.
builtin_checks.rationale: With a TCP socket and no 'tlsverify', the API accepts any client that can reach the port. 'tls' alone encrypts the channel without authenticating the caller, which is the configuration people reach for and is not sufficient.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set 'tlsverify': true with 'tlscacert', 'tlscert' and 'tlskey', and issue a client certificate per operator.

builtin_checks.title: Docker restricts traffic between containers on the default bridge
builtin_checks.description: Whether unrelated containers on the default bridge may reach each other. Unset, Docker defaults to true.
builtin_checks.rationale: With icc on, one compromised container can reach every other container's ports on the default bridge, including ones never published to the host. Lateral movement inside the estate needs no further access.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set '"icc": false' and connect containers that must talk to each other on an explicit user-defined network.

builtin_checks.title: Docker trusts no registry over plain HTTP
builtin_checks.description: Registries the daemon will contact without TLS, or whose certificate it will not verify.
builtin_checks.rationale: An image pulled over plain HTTP can be replaced in transit, and the daemon runs whatever it receives as the container's contents. A single entry here undermines image provenance for everything pulled from that host.
builtin_checks.remediation: Remove the entry and give the registry a certificate the daemon trusts.

builtin_checks.title: Docker containers cannot gain new privileges by default
builtin_checks.description: Whether the daemon applies no-new-privileges to every container by default. Unset, Docker defaults to false.
builtin_checks.rationale: Without it, a setuid binary inside a container can still raise privileges, so a container escape that depends on one stays available even where the container itself runs as a non-root user.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set '"no-new-privileges": true' and restart the daemon.

builtin_checks.title: Docker remaps container root to an unprivileged host user
builtin_checks.description: User-namespace remapping. Unset, root inside a container is root on the host.
builtin_checks.rationale: Without remapping, uid 0 in a container is uid 0 on the host, so any escape from the namespace lands as root. Remapping makes the same escape land as an unprivileged account.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set '"userns-remap": "default"' and restart. Note this breaks containers that need host-uid parity on bind mounts, so stage it.

builtin_checks.title: Docker sends container output to a defined log driver
builtin_checks.description: The default logging driver. Unset, Docker uses json-file, which writes to the host's disk.
builtin_checks.rationale: Container output is the only record of what an application did. A driver that ships it off the host is what keeps that record when the host itself is the thing being investigated.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set 'log-driver' to the collector your estate uses, and pair it with 'log-opts' limits so a chatty container cannot fill the disk.

builtin_checks.title: The Docker daemon logs at a usable level
builtin_checks.description: The daemon's own log verbosity. Unset, Docker defaults to 'info'.
builtin_checks.rationale: At 'error' and above the daemon records only its own failures. Container starts, image pulls and API calls — the entries that show what was run on the host — are logged at 'info'.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set '"log-level": "info"' and restart the daemon.

builtin_checks.title: Docker applies default resource limits to containers
builtin_checks.description: Resource limits applied to every container unless overridden. Unset, containers inherit the daemon's own limits. This counts entries, so it never reports an absent reading and the absence policy below is unreachable; it is declared because ConfigCheck requires a choice.
builtin_checks.rationale: Without a default, one container can exhaust file descriptors or processes for the whole host, taking every other container with it. The limit is what keeps a runaway workload a single-container incident.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set 'default-ulimits', for example nofile and nproc, to values your workloads fit inside.

builtin_checks.title: The nginx configuration file is not world-readable
builtin_checks.description: The mode of /etc/nginx/nginx.conf. A host that does not run nginx has no such file and is not in scope for this rule.
builtin_checks.rationale: The configuration names private keys, upstream credentials and every path the service exposes. World-readable, it hands those to any local account — including the unprivileged account the service itself runs as, which is exactly where an exploit of the service lands.
builtin_checks.remediation: chmod o-rwx /etc/nginx/nginx.conf and confirm the service account can still read it, through group ownership if necessary.

builtin_checks.title: The Apache configuration file is not world-readable
builtin_checks.description: The mode of /etc/apache2/apache2.conf. A host that does not run apache has no such file and is not in scope for this rule.
builtin_checks.rationale: The configuration names private keys, upstream credentials and every path the service exposes. World-readable, it hands those to any local account — including the unprivileged account the service itself runs as, which is exactly where an exploit of the service lands.
builtin_checks.remediation: chmod o-rwx /etc/apache2/apache2.conf and confirm the service account can still read it, through group ownership if necessary.

builtin_checks.title: The Tomcat users file is not world-readable
builtin_checks.description: The mode of /usr/local/tomcat/conf/tomcat-users.xml. A host that does not run tomcat has no such file and is not in scope for this rule.
builtin_checks.rationale: The configuration names private keys, upstream credentials and every path the service exposes. World-readable, it hands those to any local account — including the unprivileged account the service itself runs as, which is exactly where an exploit of the service lands.
builtin_checks.remediation: chmod o-rwx /usr/local/tomcat/conf/tomcat-users.xml and confirm the service account can still read it, through group ownership if necessary.

builtin_checks.title: The Docker daemon configuration is not world-writable
builtin_checks.description: The mode of /etc/docker/daemon.json. A host that does not run docker has no such file and is not in scope for this rule.
builtin_checks.rationale: The configuration names private keys, upstream credentials and every path the service exposes. World-readable, it hands those to any local account — including the unprivileged account the service itself runs as, which is exactly where an exploit of the service lands.
builtin_checks.remediation: chmod o-rwx /etc/docker/daemon.json and confirm the service account can still read it, through group ownership if necessary.

builtin_checks.title: No container runs with --privileged
builtin_checks.description: Running containers started with --privileged, which disables essentially every isolation the runtime provides.
builtin_checks.rationale: A privileged container gets all capabilities, unrestricted device access and no seccomp or AppArmor confinement. Escaping it to the host is not an exploit, it is a documented feature — mounting the host disk and chrooting into it takes two commands.
builtin_checks.remediation: Remove --privileged and grant only the specific capabilities or device the workload needs, with --cap-add and --device.

builtin_checks.title: No container shares the host PID, IPC or UTS namespace
builtin_checks.description: Containers started with --pid=host, --ipc=host or --uts=host.
builtin_checks.rationale: Sharing the host PID namespace lets the container see and signal every process on the machine, and read their memory through /proc if it has the capability. Shared IPC exposes host shared memory. Each removes a boundary the container was meant to have.
