builtin_checks.remediation: Drop the --pid, --ipc and --uts host flags. Where a monitoring agent genuinely needs process visibility, run it on the host rather than in a container pretending to be isolated.

builtin_checks.title: No container shares the host network namespace
builtin_checks.description: Containers started with --network=host.
builtin_checks.rationale: The container binds directly onto the host's interfaces, so port publishing and network policy no longer apply to it and it can reach anything the host can, including services bound to loopback that were never meant to be reachable.
builtin_checks.remediation: Use a user-defined network and publish only the ports the service needs.

builtin_checks.title: No container has the Docker socket mounted into it
builtin_checks.description: Containers with /var/run/docker.sock bind-mounted, which grants them the Docker API.
builtin_checks.rationale: The Docker API is root-equivalent on the host by design. A container holding the socket can start a privileged container that mounts the host filesystem, so this is a container escape requiring no vulnerability at all — and it is the single most common one, because CI runners and monitoring agents ask for it.
builtin_checks.remediation: Remove the bind mount. Where a workload must talk to the daemon, put a proxy in front of it that permits only the specific calls it needs.

builtin_checks.title: No container bind-mounts a sensitive host path
builtin_checks.description: Containers bind-mounting /, /etc, /proc, /sys, /boot, /dev, /root or the Docker data directory from the host.
builtin_checks.rationale: A writable mount of /etc rewrites the host's accounts and cron; a mount of / is the host filesystem. Even read-only, these hand over credentials and configuration the container had no reason to see.
builtin_checks.remediation: Mount only the specific directory the workload needs, read-only where possible.

builtin_checks.title: No container runs its process as uid 0
builtin_checks.description: Containers whose configured user is root, or which declare no user at all and therefore inherit the image's default of root.
builtin_checks.rationale: Root in the container is root on the host the moment any isolation boundary fails, and it makes every other weakness — a writable mount, an added capability — worth more to an attacker.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set USER in the image or --user at run time. Combine with --read-only and a dropped capability set.

builtin_checks.title: No container is granted a capability that reaches the host
builtin_checks.description: Containers granted SYS_ADMIN, SYS_PTRACE, SYS_MODULE, SYS_RAWIO, DAC_READ_SEARCH, NET_ADMIN or ALL. Capabilities images legitimately add, such as NET_BIND_SERVICE, are not reported.
builtin_checks.rationale: SYS_ADMIN is close to privileged on its own — it permits mounting and much of what --privileged grants. SYS_PTRACE reaches into other processes, SYS_MODULE loads kernel code, and DAC_READ_SEARCH bypasses file permission checks entirely.
builtin_checks.remediation: Drop the capability. Where one is genuinely required, record the exception and pair it with a read-only root filesystem and a non-root user.

builtin_checks.title: Containers are started with no-new-privileges
builtin_checks.description: Containers without --security-opt no-new-privileges:true.
builtin_checks.rationale: Without it a setuid binary inside the image can still raise privileges, so a container running as a non-root user is not actually confined to that user's authority.
builtin_checks.remediation: Add --security-opt no-new-privileges:true, or set it as a daemon default so every container inherits it.

builtin_checks.title: Containers run with a read-only root filesystem
builtin_checks.description: Containers whose root filesystem is writable.
builtin_checks.rationale: A writable root filesystem lets an attacker who reaches code execution drop tooling and persist inside the container. A read-only root with explicit writable volumes removes that without changing what the application can legitimately do.
builtin_checks.remediation: Add --read-only and mount tmpfs or a volume at the specific paths the application writes to.

builtin_checks.title: No workload pod runs a privileged container
builtin_checks.description: Pods outside kube-system whose containers set securityContext.privileged. The cluster's own components are excluded because several of them legitimately require it.
builtin_checks.rationale: A privileged pod has the node, not just the pod. It is the standard first step from an application compromise to control of the worker and everything scheduled on it.
builtin_checks.remediation: Remove securityContext.privileged and grant the specific capability the workload needs. Enforce it with Pod Security admission so it cannot be reintroduced.

builtin_checks.title: No workload pod shares a host namespace
builtin_checks.description: Pods outside kube-system setting hostPID, hostIPC or hostNetwork.
builtin_checks.rationale: hostNetwork puts the pod on the node's interfaces, bypassing NetworkPolicy entirely; hostPID exposes every process on the node. Both remove a boundary the cluster's other controls assume is there.
builtin_checks.remediation: Remove the host namespace flags and enforce the 'baseline' or 'restricted' Pod Security standard on the namespace.

builtin_checks.title: Workload pods declare that they do not run as root
builtin_checks.description: Pods outside kube-system that set neither runAsNonRoot nor a non-zero runAsUser, at pod or container level.
builtin_checks.rationale: A pod that says nothing runs as whatever uid the image declares, which for most images is 0. Declaring runAsNonRoot makes the kubelet refuse to start a container that would run as root, which turns an image regression into a failed deployment rather than a silent privilege increase.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set securityContext.runAsNonRoot: true and a runAsUser, and enforce it through Pod Security admission.

builtin_checks.title: Namespaces enforce a Pod Security standard
builtin_checks.description: Namespaces with no pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce label. The cluster's own namespaces are excluded.
builtin_checks.rationale: Pod Security admission is opt-in per namespace. Without the enforce label the namespace admits privileged pods, host namespaces and host path mounts regardless of any other policy, so every workload rule above becomes advisory.
builtin_checks.remediation: Label the namespace pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=baseline (or restricted), after checking existing workloads against it with the warn label.

builtin_checks.title: cluster-admin is not bound beyond the cluster's own bindings
builtin_checks.description: Subjects bound to the cluster-admin ClusterRole, excluding the binding Kubernetes creates for system:masters.
builtin_checks.rationale: cluster-admin is unbounded authority over every resource in every namespace, including secrets and the RBAC rules themselves. A ServiceAccount holding it turns any pod running under it into full cluster control.
builtin_checks.remediation: Remove the binding and grant a role scoped to what the subject actually needs, namespaced where possible.

builtin_checks.title: No custom role grants wildcard verbs on wildcard resources
builtin_checks.description: Roles and ClusterRoles granting '*' verbs on '*' resources. Roles Kubernetes ships are excluded by their bootstrapping label — cluster-admin legitimately holds exactly this.
builtin_checks.rationale: A wildcard on both axes is authority over resource kinds that do not exist yet: install a CRD next month and the role covers it. It cannot be reasoned about from a review of what exists today.
builtin_checks.remediation: Enumerate the apiGroups, resources and verbs the subject needs. Where a wildcard is unavoidable, confine it to one apiGroup.

builtin_checks.title: Default ServiceAccounts do not automount their token
builtin_checks.description: Default ServiceAccounts outside the cluster's own namespaces that have not set automountServiceAccountToken: false.
builtin_checks.rationale: The default ServiceAccount exists in every namespace and its token is projected into any pod that does not opt out. A container compromise therefore hands over an API credential the workload never asked for and probably does not use.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set automountServiceAccountToken: false on the default ServiceAccount in each namespace, and mount a token explicitly for the workloads that genuinely call the API.

builtin_checks.title: The cluster enforces RBAC authorization
builtin_checks.description: Whether the API server serves the rbac.authorization.k8s.io group. It does not when RBAC is disabled, which is the observable — the API server's own flags are not readable on every distribution.
builtin_checks.rationale: Without RBAC the API server authorises by another mode, and the common alternative on a misconfigured cluster is AlwaysAllow: every authenticated request succeeds, and every role and binding in the cluster is decoration.
builtin_checks.remediation: Start the API server with --authorization-mode including RBAC. On a managed or embedded distribution this is a cluster setting rather than a flag.

builtin_checks.title: The kubelet refuses anonymous requests
builtin_checks.description: Whether the kubelet accepts unauthenticated requests to its API. Unset, the kubelet's own default is true; kubeadm writes false.
builtin_checks.rationale: The kubelet API can list pods, read their logs and — with authorization also permissive — exec into containers. Anonymous access to it is unauthenticated access to every workload on the node.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set authentication.anonymous.enabled: false in the kubelet configuration and restart the kubelet.

builtin_checks.title: The kubelet authorizes requests through the API server
builtin_checks.description: The kubelet's authorization mode. Unset, the kubelet defaults to AlwaysAllow; kubeadm writes Webhook.
builtin_checks.rationale: AlwaysAllow means every request the kubelet authenticates is also authorised, so anyone who can present any valid credential gets everything the kubelet API offers. Webhook delegates the decision to the API server's RBAC.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set authorization.mode: Webhook and restart the kubelet.

builtin_checks.title: The kubelet read-only port is disabled
builtin_checks.description: The unauthenticated read-only kubelet port. Unset, the kubelet's own default is 10255 in older releases and 0 in current ones.
builtin_checks.rationale: The read-only port serves pod and node state with no authentication at all. It is a complete inventory of what runs on the node, including environment variables, to anyone who can reach the port.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set readOnlyPort: 0 and restart the kubelet.

builtin_checks.title: The kubelet verifies client certificates against a CA
builtin_checks.description: The certificate authority the kubelet validates client certificates against. Unset, x509 client authentication is not available and the kubelet falls back to its other authenticators.
builtin_checks.rationale: Without a client CA the kubelet cannot distinguish the API server from anything else presenting a certificate, so certificate-based authentication to it establishes nothing.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set authentication.x509.clientCAFile to the cluster CA and restart the kubelet.

builtin_checks.title: The kubelet rotates its client certificate
builtin_checks.description: Whether the kubelet requests a new client certificate as the current one approaches expiry. Unset, the kubelet defaults to true in current releases.
builtin_checks.rationale: Without rotation the node's credential is long-lived, so a copy taken from a compromised node stays usable for the life of the certificate rather than for hours.
builtin_checks.remediation: Set rotateCertificates: true and restart the kubelet.

builtin_checks.title: The containerd configuration is present and parseable
builtin_checks.description: containerd's configuration schema version. Version 1 was removed in containerd 2.0, so a host still on it is running a configuration the current daemon will not read.
builtin_checks.rationale: A configuration the daemon silently ignores means every setting in it — including the registry and sandbox settings the checks below read — is not in force, while looking as though it is.
builtin_checks.remediation: Migrate the configuration to version 2 with 'containerd config migrate', or regenerate it with 'containerd config default'.

builtin_checks.title: containerd verifies TLS for every registry mirror
builtin_checks.description: Registries with a per-registry TLS configuration block. Such a block is where insecure_skip_verify is set, and its absence means containerd verifies every mirror normally.
builtin_checks.rationale: A registry configured with insecure_skip_verify accepts any certificate, so an image pulled from it can be replaced in transit — and containerd runs whatever it receives as the container's contents.
builtin_checks.remediation: Remove the per-registry TLS override and give the registry a certificate the host trusts. Where a private CA is used, add it to the host trust store rather than disabling verification.

network_checks.title: Deprecated TLS/SSL protocol version offered
network_checks.description: The service negotiates a protocol version that is no longer considered secure. SSLv2 and SSLv3 are broken; TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are withdrawn and rely on primitives with no remaining security margin.
network_checks.remediation: Disable SSLv2, SSLv3, TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 on this listener and offer TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 only.

network_checks.title: No modern TLS protocol offered
network_checks.description: The service offers neither TLS 1.2 nor TLS 1.3, so every connection it accepts is negotiated on a withdrawn protocol.
network_checks.remediation: Enable TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 on this listener.

network_checks.title: Weak TLS cipher suite offered
network_checks.description: The service offers cipher suites built on primitives that are broken or have no security margin left — RC4, single DES, 3DES, EXPORT grades, anonymous key exchange, or NULL encryption.
network_checks.remediation: Restrict the cipher list to AEAD suites (AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305) with forward secrecy, and remove RC4, DES, 3DES, EXPORT, anon and NULL suites.

network_checks.title: TLS certificate has expired
network_checks.description: The certificate presented by this service is past its notAfter date. Clients cannot distinguish an expired certificate from an intercepted connection, so users are trained to click through the warning that would otherwise stop an active attacker.
network_checks.remediation: Renew the certificate and automate renewal before expiry.

network_checks.title: TLS certificate is self-signed
network_checks.description: The certificate's subject and issuer are identical, so no authority vouches for it. A client has no way to tell it from a certificate an interceptor generated.
network_checks.remediation: Issue the certificate from a CA the clients trust. Where a public CA cannot be used, deploy an internal CA and distribute its root to every client.

network_checks.title: TLS certificate signed with a weak algorithm
network_checks.description: The certificate is signed with MD5 or SHA-1. Collisions against both are practical, so the signature no longer binds the key to the name.
network_checks.remediation: Re-issue the certificate with a SHA-256 or stronger signature.

network_checks.title: TLS certificate does not match the host
network_checks.description: Neither the certificate's subject nor any subjectAltName entry matches the address the service was reached on, so hostname verification cannot succeed for a client using that address.
network_checks.remediation: Re-issue the certificate with every name and address clients use in its subjectAltName extension.

network_checks.title: OpenSSL Heartbleed memory disclosure
network_checks.description: The service answers a malformed TLS heartbeat with more data than it was sent, disclosing adjacent process memory — which can contain private keys, session tokens and credentials.
network_checks.remediation: Upgrade OpenSSL to 1.0.1g or later and rotate every key and credential the affected process held.

network_checks.title: Bleichenbacher RSA oracle (ROBOT)
network_checks.description: The service leaks distinguishable errors for malformed RSA key-exchange messages, which allows an attacker to decrypt recorded sessions or forge signatures with the server's key.
network_checks.remediation: Disable RSA key-exchange cipher suites, or apply the vendor patch for the TLS stack in use.

network_checks.title: TLS compression enabled (CRIME)
network_checks.description: TLS-level compression is enabled. An attacker able to inject chosen plaintext into a connection can recover secrets from it by observing compressed record lengths.
network_checks.remediation: Disable TLS compression on this listener.

network_checks.title: Server certificate does not chain to a trusted root
network_checks.description: The certificate could not be validated against any trust store: the chain is broken, an intermediate is missing, or the issuer is not publicly trusted. A client cannot distinguish this from an interception, so users are trained to click through the warning.
network_checks.remediation: Serve the full chain including intermediates, or replace the certificate with one issued by a CA the clients trust. A deliberately private CA is a legitimate answer — distribute its root to the clients that need it.

network_checks.title: Certificate chain is sent out of order
network_checks.description: The certificates were presented in an order RFC 8446 does not permit. Most clients tolerate it; some embedded and older stacks do not, and the failure they produce looks like an expired certificate rather than a misordered one.
network_checks.remediation: Concatenate the leaf first, then each issuer in turn.

network_checks.title: SHA-1 signature in the verified certificate chain
network_checks.description: A certificate in the validated chain is signed with SHA-1, which is collision-vulnerable and rejected by current browsers. This is distinct from the leaf's own signature: the weakness can sit on an intermediate the operator did not choose.
network_checks.remediation: Reissue from a chain signed with SHA-256 or better; ask the CA for a cross-signed intermediate if the old one is still served.

network_checks.title: Server certificate is not yet valid
network_checks.description: notBefore is in the future, so every correctly behaving client refuses this certificate. Usually a clock skew on the issuing host, or a certificate deployed ahead of its start date.
network_checks.remediation: Correct the server clock, or wait for the validity window to open. If the certificate was issued early, reissue it.

network_checks.title: Server certificate uses a key below the modern floor
network_checks.description: The public key is smaller than current guidance permits — under 2048 bits for RSA or DSA, under 224 for an elliptic curve. The certificate's strength bounds the session's, whatever suite is negotiated.
network_checks.remediation: Reissue with a 2048-bit RSA key or a P-256 curve, at least.

network_checks.title: Server staples no OCSP response
network_checks.description: Without a stapled response every client must reach the CA itself to learn whether the certificate is revoked — which leaks who is visiting, and which most clients silently skip when it fails.
network_checks.remediation: Enable OCSP stapling on the listener.

network_checks.title: Certificate requires OCSP stapling and the server provides none
network_checks.description: The certificate carries the must-staple extension, which instructs clients to refuse the connection if no OCSP response is stapled — and the server staples none. Clients that honour the extension cannot connect at all.
network_checks.remediation: Enable OCSP stapling, or reissue without the must-staple extension. Leaving it as it is means an outage for correct clients.

network_checks.title: Listener does not honour TLS_FALLBACK_SCSV
network_checks.description: The server ignores the fallback signalling cipher suite, so it cannot tell a genuine retry from an attacker forcing a downgrade. On a listener that still offers an older protocol version, this is what makes the downgrade reachable.
network_checks.remediation: Upgrade the TLS library to one supporting RFC 7507, and remove the older protocol versions the downgrade would target.

network_checks.title: Client-initiated renegotiation is permitted
network_checks.description: A client can ask the server to renegotiate repeatedly on one connection. The asymmetry is the problem: each renegotiation costs the server a key exchange and the client almost nothing, so one connection can consume disproportionate CPU.
network_checks.remediation: Disable client-initiated renegotiation. Most modern stacks refuse it by default; a server permitting it is usually running an older OpenSSL or an explicit override.

network_checks.title: Ephemeral ECDH group is below the modern floor
network_checks.description: An accepted suite negotiates an elliptic-curve group under 224 bits. The suite name says ECDHE and looks modern; only the group size says how much security it actually provides.
network_checks.remediation: Restrict the curve list to P-256, P-384, X25519 or better.

network_checks.title: No forward-secret cipher suite is offered
network_checks.description: Every accepted suite uses static key exchange, so one compromise of the server's private key decrypts all past traffic that was ever captured — including traffic recorded before the key leaked.
network_checks.remediation: Offer ECDHE or DHE suites and prefer them. On TLS 1.3 this is automatic; on 1.2 it is a cipher-list change.

network_checks.title: OpenSSL ChangeCipherSpec injection (CVE-2014-0224)
network_checks.description: The server accepts a ChangeCipherSpec message early in the handshake, letting an attacker in the path force both sides onto predictable keying material and read or alter the session.
network_checks.remediation: Upgrade OpenSSL to 1.0.1h or later.

network_checks.title: TLS 1.3 0-RTT early data is accepted
network_checks.description: The server accepts early data, which has no replay protection at the TLS layer. An observer can resend a captured 0-RTT payload; whether that matters depends on whether the application treats the request as idempotent.
network_checks.remediation: Disable 0-RTT, or confirm that every endpoint reachable through early data is safe to replay.

network_checks.title: Extended master secret is not supported
network_checks.description: Without RFC 7627 the master secret is not bound to the full handshake, which is what the triple-handshake attack exploits to make two distinct sessions share keying material.
network_checks.remediation: Enable the extended master secret extension, or move to TLS 1.3.

network_checks.title: Server certificate expires within 30 days
network_checks.description: The certificate is still valid, so this is not yet an outage — which is exactly why it is worth reporting now rather than on the morning it stops working.
network_checks.remediation: Renew the certificate and confirm automated renewal is running.

network_checks.title: Ephemeral Diffie-Hellman group is too small (Logjam)
network_checks.description: An accepted suite negotiates a DH group under 2048 bits. Groups at 1024 bits and below are precomputable by a well-resourced attacker, and the 512-bit export groups are breakable outright.
network_checks.remediation: Generate a 2048-bit or larger DH parameter file, or drop DHE in favour of ECDHE.

network_checks.title: Secure renegotiation (RFC 5746) is not supported
network_checks.description: The listener does not support the renegotiation indication extension, so an attacker in the path can prefix their own plaintext to a client's session — the 2009 TLS renegotiation flaw.
network_checks.remediation: Upgrade the TLS library; every current one supports RFC 5746.

network_checks.title: HTTP security headers absent
network_checks.description: The response omits one or more headers browsers rely on to constrain the page — Strict-Transport-Security, Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options. Their absence is not itself an exploitable flaw; it removes the defences that would limit one.
network_checks.remediation: Set the missing headers at the server or reverse proxy. Note that an nginx `location` block containing any add_header replaces the parent's whole set, so headers declared at server level must be repeated inside it.

network_checks.title: Service offered over cleartext HTTP
network_checks.description: The service answers on plain HTTP, so anything it carries — session cookies, credentials, form data — is readable and modifiable by anyone on the path.
network_checks.remediation: Terminate TLS in front of this service and redirect HTTP to HTTPS permanently.

network_checks.title: Session cookie missing HttpOnly or Secure
network_checks.description: A cookie is set without HttpOnly, leaving it readable by script, or without Secure on a cleartext connection, allowing it to be captured in transit.
network_checks.remediation: Set HttpOnly and Secure on every session cookie, and SameSite where the application allows.

network_checks.title: Sensitive file exposed over HTTP
network_checks.description: A file that should never be web-reachable is served with content matching its expected format — an environment file, a version control directory, a PHP information page or a server status endpoint. These routinely contain credentials, internal hostnames or the application's source layout.
network_checks.remediation: Remove the file from the document root, or deny it at the web server. Rotate any credential the exposed content disclosed.

network_checks.title: Directory listing enabled
network_checks.description: The server returns an index of a directory's contents instead of a document, disclosing filenames that were not meant to be enumerable.
network_checks.remediation: Disable automatic directory indexing (`autoindex off`, `Options -Indexes`).

network_checks.title: Dangerous HTTP methods accepted
network_checks.description: The server accepts PUT, DELETE or TRACE. The first two can modify content where authorisation is misconfigured; TRACE reflects the request and enables cross-site tracing.
network_checks.remediation: Restrict the accepted method set to those the application needs, typically GET, HEAD and POST.

network_checks.title: Server header discloses a product version
network_checks.description: The Server response header names the product and its version, which tells an attacker exactly which published vulnerabilities to try without probing for them.
network_checks.remediation: Suppress the version in the Server header (`server_tokens off`, `ServerTokens Prod`).

network_checks.title: Default HTTP credentials accepted
network_checks.description: The service accepted a documented default username and password over HTTP Basic authentication, granting whatever access that account holds.
network_checks.remediation: Change the account's password immediately and audit what the account has been used for.

network_checks.title: Bash Shellshock via CGI
network_checks.description: A CGI endpoint passes attacker-controlled headers into a Bash environment that evaluates trailing function definitions, giving unauthenticated command execution.
network_checks.remediation: Patch Bash to a version that rejects the trailing-function parse, and disable unused CGI handlers.

network_checks.title: Anonymous FTP login accepted
network_checks.description: The server accepted a login as `anonymous`, so its exported contents are readable by anyone who can reach the port.
network_checks.remediation: Disable anonymous access, or confine it to a directory holding only material intended to be public.

network_checks.title: Anonymous FTP session has write access
network_checks.description: An anonymous session was able to create a directory. Anyone who can reach the port can place files on this host, which on a server that also serves them over HTTP is remote code execution.
network_checks.remediation: Remove write permission from the anonymous FTP root immediately.

network_checks.title: FTP accepts documented default credentials
network_checks.description: The server accepted a username and password pair from the published default-credential lists, granting that account's access to anyone who can reach the port.
network_checks.remediation: Change the account's password immediately, or disable the account if it is unused.

network_checks.title: FTP transmits credentials in cleartext
network_checks.description: FTP carries its control channel, including the USER and PASS commands, without encryption. This is a property of the protocol rather than of this server's configuration, so it is reported at low severity: it is true of every FTP service and states a risk rather than a proven weakness.
network_checks.remediation: Replace FTP with SFTP or FTPS.

network_checks.title: SMBv1 offered by the server
network_checks.description: The server answered an SMBv1 negotiate with an SMBv1 response, so the deprecated dialect is still enabled. SMBv1 has no protection against downgrade or relay and is the dialect the MS17-010 family of vulnerabilities is reached through.
network_checks.remediation: Disable the SMBv1 client and server components and confirm no remaining device requires them.

network_checks.title: SMB signing not required
network_checks.description: The server does not require SMB message signing, so an attacker positioned on the path can relay an authentication exchange to a third host and act as the authenticating user.
network_checks.remediation: Require SMB signing on both server and client.

network_checks.title: MS17-010 SMBv1 remote code execution (EternalBlue)
network_checks.description: The SMBv1 server responds in the way an unpatched MS17-010 host does, which permits unauthenticated remote code execution as SYSTEM.
network_checks.remediation: Apply MS17-010 and disable SMBv1.

network_checks.title: SNMP accepts a default or guessable community string
network_checks.description: The agent answered a query authenticated by a community string taken from the published default list. The community string is SNMP's only access control in v1 and v2c.
network_checks.remediation: Replace the community string with an unguessable value, restrict the agent to known managers by source address, and move to SNMPv3 with authentication and privacy.

network_checks.title: SNMPv1/v2c in use — community sent in cleartext
network_checks.description: The agent answered an SNMPv1/v2c request. Both versions send the community string unencrypted, so anyone on the path learns the credential by observing one poll.
network_checks.remediation: Move to SNMPv3 with authPriv and disable v1 and v2c.

network_checks.title: SNMP discloses system and network detail without authentication
network_checks.description: The agent returned system description, interface table or IP address table content to an unauthenticated query. Together these map the device's software version and its internal addressing.
network_checks.remediation: Restrict the agent to known managers, limit the exposed view to the OIDs monitoring needs, and move to SNMPv3.

network_checks.title: SSH offers weak key exchange, cipher or MAC algorithms
network_checks.description: The server's algorithm proposal includes primitives with no remaining security margin — SHA-1 based key exchange, RC4, single-DES or Blowfish ciphers, or MD5 and truncated SHA-1 MACs. A client that negotiates one of them gets a session an attacker recording traffic may later be able to read.
network_checks.remediation: Restrict KexAlgorithms, Ciphers and MACs in sshd_config to the modern set, then restart sshd.

network_checks.title: Telnet reachable — credentials in cleartext
network_checks.description: Telnet is listening. It carries authentication and session data without encryption, so credentials are recoverable by anyone on the path.
network_checks.remediation: Disable Telnet and use SSH.

network_checks.title: Redis accepts commands without authentication
network_checks.description: The Redis instance executed a command from an unauthenticated connection, so its entire dataset is readable and writable by anyone who can reach the port.
network_checks.remediation: Set requirepass, bind the instance to a loopback or private interface, and enable protected-mode.

network_checks.title: MongoDB accepts unauthenticated access
network_checks.description: The MongoDB instance answered a query from an unauthenticated connection, so every database it holds can be read and modified.
network_checks.remediation: Enable authorization, create administrative users, and bind the instance to a private interface.

network_checks.title: MQTT broker accepts anonymous connections
network_checks.description: The broker accepted a connection with no credentials, so any reachable client can subscribe to every topic and publish to it.
network_checks.remediation: Disable anonymous access, require credentials, and apply per-topic access control.

network_checks.title: Memcached reachable without authentication
network_checks.description: The instance answered an unauthenticated request. Beyond exposing whatever is cached, a memcached instance reachable over UDP is a high-ratio traffic amplification source.
network_checks.remediation: Bind to a private interface, disable the UDP listener, and enable SASL authentication.

network_checks.title: Directory readable via anonymous bind
network_checks.description: The directory accepted an anonymous bind and returned data. Directory content typically enumerates every account, group and organisational unit, which is the reconnaissance an attacker needs before a credential attack.
network_checks.remediation: Disable anonymous bind, or restrict what an anonymous bind may read to the root DSE.

network_checks.title: DNS zone transfer permitted to an arbitrary client
network_checks.description: The server answered an AXFR request, returning the zone's full record set — every hostname, address and service record it holds.
network_checks.remediation: Restrict zone transfers to the secondary nameservers by address, and require TSIG.

network_checks.title: DNS server performs recursion for arbitrary clients
network_checks.description: The server resolved a name it is not authoritative for on behalf of an arbitrary client, which makes it usable as a reflector in amplification attacks and exposes its cache to poisoning.
network_checks.remediation: Restrict recursion to the client networks the resolver serves.

network_checks.title: CVE candidates from fingerprinted service versions
network_checks.description: Published CVEs whose affected version range contains the version fingerprinted on a listening service. Each finding files under its own real CVE identifier.

network_checks.title: Conditions verified by an active Nuclei template
network_checks.description: A template matched a live response, so the condition is present and reachable now. A CVE-tagged template files under that CVE; a template with no CVE files under a minted CCURE-CHK- identifier carrying its template id.
